observations.fact: A new axi_transfer is created on AW/W/B/AR/R and AW2B/AR2R completion paths and written to analysis ports; W and R transfers carry byte queues. Delay queues push at AW/AR and pop at B/R.
The monitor analysis ports connect synchronously to axi_state implementations; state.item_wtr_port and item_rtr_port pass completed transfers onward.

Per-ID AW/W/B/AR/R and read-model queues hold pending transfer handles. AW/W merges move handles to B response queues and completed B paths pop them. AR creates a cloned read-model transfer; R data consumption pops its model queue at last segment, and AR/R assembled transfer is popped on AR2R. bq_rsp and bq_for_rsp_lat briefly share a handle until their respective pops.
Completed W/R callbacks synchronously call reference_model and scoreboard; the monitor has no additional transaction queue.
AXI write/read callback bodies are empty; scoreboard retains no explicit per-access transaction collection.
AXI write callbacks send transfer byte data/address into page memory writes; AXI read callbacks are empty.
Each transfer object has dynamic queues for data, byte addresses, strobe, response and delay; pending bursts can therefore have host cost beyond payload bytes.
